🇬🇧 ⚡️ For the first time since the Cold War, the British Ministry of Defence has sent letters to approximately 100,000 reservists, urging them to prepare for the possibility of being called up for military service in the event of a war, according to The Telegraph… The British Ministry of Defense is preparing for a possible mobilization but cannot locate half of its reservists, reports The Times. London has begun sending letters to former regular servicemen asking them to be ready for conscription, but of the 95,000 people in the strategic reserve, only 50,000 could be contacted. For the first time since the Cold War, former servicemen are being asked to update their contact details and information about their professional skills in case of mobilization. They are also invited to participate in exercises. Defense Minister Streeting stated that these measures are a necessary precaution due to the threat from Russia. The British Parliament is discussing raising the maximum conscription age for certain categories of reservists from 55 to 65 and the possibility of their mobilization even at the stage of preparation for war. @americanmajority
